messages:
sarah_support: FYI customer reported a sudden spike of 502s for a single tenant (redscale) hitting hosted API between 14:02-14:12 UTC, ~25% error rate on generation and embeddings calls. attaching their sample req id list they sent.

mike_ops: can you paste a couple of request_ids + any edge trace ids? also which path — /v1/embeddings or /v1/generate? :eyes:

sarah_support: they reported both, but most noisy on /v1/embeddings. sample ids: req_01a2, req_01a3, req_01a7. customer says it started after they rolled a client that batches 512 vectors into one request.

raj_engineer: quick glance at edge logs for those req ids: envoy->upstream reset for the upstream pool. excerpt: 
```
[envoy][2026-06-15T14:04:12Z] router dispatch failure: upstream reset: connection failure or reset by peer
upstream_host: 10.12.8.22:8443, x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 12001
```
Also see consistent header: "x-tenant-id: redscale" on failing requests.

tess_prodeng: interesting — redscale has a lot of concurrent big-batch embedding requests from one instance. could be per-tenant mux queue starvation: too many inflight requests queued, upstream pool hits conn/stream limits and envoy returns 502.

mike_ops: can we reproduce locally with a heavy batch? try a curl with many vectors. I put a minimal repro below (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "x-tenant-id: redscale" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-1","inputs": ["v1","v2",...,"v512"]}' \
  https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/embeddings
```
I ran something similar and hit 502s when concurrency > 30.

raj_engineer: confirms — reproduced locally against staging pool with 512-batch and 40 parallel clients. Envoy logs show stream reset and upstream connection refused after queue flush. Root cause likely queue overflow + per-upstream conn limit. Not seeing auth errors or billing header oddities.

sarah_support: customer also sent edge proxy capture: shows chunked transfer with large body and keepalive window clumping many streams onto same backend host.

tess_prodeng: mitigation options: 1) short term: add tenant-specific rate-limit to cap concurrent embeddings requests for redscale (throttle to 10 concurrent), 2) medium term: suggestion to move redscale to dedicated pool or increase pool size & per-tenant concurrency, 3) longer term: make mux queue backpressure earlier and return 429 instead of letting envoy drop to 502.

mike_ops: I'm going to push a temporary per-tenant ratelimit rule for redscale and also bump the upstream conn limit on the pool behind the affected frontdoor. infra-bot will post when rule is live.

infra-bot: applied ACL/rate-limit rule: path=/v1/embeddings, header x-tenant-id=redscale, concurrency=10, scope=60s. Rule deployment id: rl-20260615-33. :white_check_mark:

mike_ops: after rule we saw error rate drop from 25% -> 1.8% for that tenant. customer confirmed fewer 502s in last 10m. :thumbsup:

raj_engineer: adding follow-ups: add per-tenant queue depth metric, expose histogram for envoys that maps queue depth -> 5xx rate, and add a circuit-breaker that prefers 429 when local queue > threshold. will open jira.

tess_prodeng: also recommend a docs blurb in "best practices for batching" — warn about single-tenant large-batch storms and provide suggested client-side concurrency caps.

sarah_support: customer-facing note: asked redscale to roll back client change to smaller batch size (<=128) as a safer immediate step. they acknowledged.

mike_ops: created incident follow-up ticket INF-3891 with log excerpts, repro script, and mitigation applied. assigning to raj_engineer for a fix and tess_prodeng for docs.

raj_engineer: will investigate whether we can route large-body requests across more backends (avoid single-host clumping) and whether NGINX/Envoy pool sizing defaults are optimal for embeddings path.

tess_prodeng: next steps done: runbook note -> include curl repro and quick mitigation steps (apply tenant rate-limit, ask customer to lower batch size, route to dedicated pool).

sarah_support: closing thread, will ping if customer sees regression. thanks all. :heart:
